Challenge 3: Caccetta–Häggkvist Conjecture

Given a simple digraph, if each vertex has an out-neighbour, then it contains a directed cycle [1], but not necessarily a short one. As the minimum out-degree increases, girth is expected to decrease. A natural construction is the digraph on n cyclically ordered vertices, where each vertex is joined to the next r vertices. In this example, the minimum out-degree is r and the girth is ⌈n/r⌉. The Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture asserts that no digraph with minimum out-degree r can do better.

Conjecture 1.1 (Caccetta–Häggkvist Conjecture [2]).

Let r∈ℕ with r≥1. Every simple directed graph on n vertices with minimum out-degree at least r has a cycle of length at most ⌈n/r⌉.

For r=1 the statement is elementary. The conjecture was proved for r=2 by Caccetta and Häggkvist [2], for r=3 by Hamidoune [3], and for r=4 and r=5 by Hoàng and Reed [4]. Shen proved it for every r under the additional assumption n≥2⁢r2−3⁢r+1 [5].

References

  • [1] J. Bang-Jensen and G. Gutin (2009) Digraphs: theory, algorithms and applications. 2 edition, Springer Monographs in Mathematics, Springer.
  • [2] L. Caccetta and R. Häggkvist (1978) On minimal digraphs with given girth. In Proceedings of the Ninth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and Computing (Boca Raton, 1978), Congressus Numerantium, Vol. 21, pp. 181–187.
  • [3] Y. O. Hamidoune (1987) A note on minimal directed graphs with given girth. Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 43 (3), pp. 343–348.
  • [4] C. T. Hoàng and B. Reed (1987) A note on short cycles in digraphs. Discrete Mathematics 66 (1–2), pp. 103–107.
  • [5] J. Shen (2000) On the girth of digraphs. Discrete Mathematics 211 (1–3), pp. 167–181.
